# E0230: `use` of an item

`use` imports a module, never an item: write `use std.sync`, then name the item through the module, as `sync.Shared`.

- Rule: [`program.what-use-binds`](../../reference/04-programs.md#program.what-use-binds)
- Reported at: the `use` declaration.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `items` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0230:1
use std.sync.Shared

fn counter() -> Shared<i64> { Shared.new(0) }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
use std.sync

fn counter() -> sync.Shared<i64> { sync.Shared.new(0) }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0230_use_of_an_item.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0230_use_of_an_item.lt):

```text
── `use` OF AN ITEM ─────────────────────── E0230_use_of_an_item.lt:1:1  [E0230]

`use` names a module: write `use std.sync`, then `sync.Shared`:

  1 │ use std.sync.Shared
    │ ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

`use` imports a module, never an item: write `use std.sync`, then name the item
through the module, as `sync.Shared`.

To fix it, import `std.sync`:

  1 │ use std.sync
    │ ~~~~~~~~~~~~
```
